description: Phase A test track: known-bad scenarios for Flare's stability guards. Each scenario carries its fault plan as flare_fault.json inside the job payload, so one broken worker image serves the whole catalog without a restart.
assumptions: The stack runs with the broken worker image (docker-compose.testbed.yml).
OPENROUTER_API_KEY is empty, so no model is called and no diff is produced. Only the preflight and verify phases run, which is exactly the pre-approval and post-approval half of the lifecycle.
Payload sources are syntactically valid Python unless a scenario is explicitly about the syntax guard: without a model patch the submitted candidate itself passes through postflight verification.
DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECONDS is 0, otherwise a repeated run returns the first job instead of a fresh one.
A non-timeout failure before approval ends as 'failed', while the same failure after approval ends as 'rolled_back'. That asymmetry is deliberate and pinned here.
